meta.name: Best Hypoallergenic Dog Breeds
meta.excerpt: If dog allergies have kept you from owning a dog, these breeds may be the answer. Discover the top 10 hypoallergenic dog breeds that produce less dander and shed minimally, from the elegant Poodle to the hairless Xoloitzcuintli.
meta.meta_description: Find the best hypoallergenic dog breeds for allergy sufferers. From Poodles to Xoloitzcuintlis, discover low-shedding breeds that are easier to live with.

intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Best Hypoallergenic Dog Breeds
intro.html:
No dog breed is completely allergen-free — the term "hypoallergenic" is technically a misnomer. Dog allergies are primarily triggered not by fur itself but by a protein called Can f 1, which is found in dog saliva, urine, and dander (dead skin cells). All dogs produce these proteins to some degree. However, certain breeds produce less dander, shed minimally, and are therefore far less likely to trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. For the millions of people who want a dog but struggle with allergies, these low-shedding breeds can make the dream of dog ownership a reality.

The breeds most commonly described as hypoallergenic tend to share certain coat characteristics. Many have hair rather than fur — a distinction that matters because hair grows in longer cycles and sheds far less continuously than the double coats common in heavy-shedding breeds. Others, like the Xoloitzcuintli (Mexican Hairless), have minimal or no coat at all, drastically reducing the amount of dander distributed around the home. Curly-coated breeds like the Poodle and Lagotto Romagnolo trap loose hair and dander in their curls rather than releasing it into the air, which also helps allergy sufferers.

It's important for anyone with dog allergies to spend time with a specific dog of the breed they're considering before bringing one home. Reactions can vary significantly between individual dogs even within the same breed, and personal sensitivity levels differ widely. Regular grooming, bathing, and vacuuming also play a significant role in managing allergens in the home. With the right breed and a proactive approach to cleanliness, many people with mild to moderate dog allergies find they can live comfortably with a dog from this list.

care.label: Breeds
care.heading: Top Hypoallergenic Dog Breeds
care.html:
Standard Poodle

Large60–90 min10–18 yrs lifespan

The Poodle's curly, non-shedding coat made it a natural choice for those with allergies, but the breed's intelligence and trainability are equally impressive. Originally a water retriever, the Standard Poodle is one of the most capable and adaptable breeds across dog sports, therapy work, and family life.

Full guide →

Portuguese Water Dog

Medium60–90 min11–13 yrs lifespan

The Portuguese Water Dog's wavy or curly coat sheds minimally, making it a popular choice for allergy sufferers. Bred to work alongside fishermen off the Portuguese coast, they are athletic, intelligent, and highly trainable with a strong affinity for water and an enthusiastic work ethic.

Full guide →

Bichon Frise

Small30 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Bichon Frise's fluffy white coat produces minimal shedding and low dander, making it one of the most allergy-friendly small breeds. Cheerful, adaptable, and endlessly affectionate, Bichons are ideal companions for apartment dwellers and families who want a social, low-shedding dog.

Full guide →

Maltese

Small20–30 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Maltese's long, silky coat is single-layered and sheds almost nothing, making it exceptionally friendly for allergy sufferers. This ancient companion breed from Malta has been prized for centuries for its gentle, affectionate temperament and manageable size in any living environment.

Full guide →

Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier

Medium45–60 min12–15 yrs lifespan

The Wheaten's soft, silky coat sheds minimally compared to most dogs, making it a practical choice for mild allergy sufferers. An all-purpose Irish farm dog, Wheatens balance terrier energy and independence with genuine affection and an adaptable temperament suited to active families.

Full guide →

Kerry Blue Terrier

MediumHigh12–15 yr lifespan

The Kerry Blue's distinctive wavy coat is low-shedding and produces less dander than many breeds, making it a reasonable choice for allergy sufferers. Ireland's national dog is intelligent, loyal, and versatile—formerly used for herding, hunting, and retrieving across the Irish countryside.

Full guide →

Lagotto Romagnolo

Medium60–90 min15–17 yrs lifespan

The Lagotto's thick, curly coat is woolly in texture and sheds very little, making it one of the more allergy-friendly medium breeds. Originally bred as a water retriever in the Italian Romagna region, they are now world-famous as truffle hunters, combining an extraordinary nose with eager trainability.

Full guide →

Spanish Water Dog

Medium60–90 min12–14 yrs lifespan

The Spanish Water Dog's curly, woolly coat forms natural cords that are low-shedding and hypoallergenic by nature. A versatile working breed from the Iberian Peninsula used for herding, hunting, and fishing assistance. Athletic, intelligent, and loyal to their family.

Full guide →

Xoloitzcuintli

Toy / Mini / Standard30–60 min13–18 yrs lifespan

The Xolo is one of the world's oldest and rarest breeds, and the hairless variety is essentially allergen-free with no coat to trap dander or shed. Mexico's national dog comes in three sizes and two varieties—hairless and coated—and is a loyal, calm, and dignified companion.

Full guide →

Chinese Crested

MediumModerate13–18 yr lifespan

The hairless Chinese Crested produces minimal dander and has no coat to shed, making it among the most hypoallergenic breeds available. Affectionate and social, they form close bonds with their owners. The hairless variety requires sunscreen and skin care, while the Powder Puff has a full soft coat.

Full guide →

Also Worth Considering: Designer Crossbreeds

Doodle hybrids are the modern low-allergen choice for households that want a friendly retriever- or herding-type temperament with a Poodle coat. Coat outcomes vary by generation - F1B and multigen produce the most reliably low-shedding dogs, while F1 outcomes are unpredictable. All six doodle hybrids covered on Wooffy:

  • Goldendoodle — Golden Retriever x Poodle. Friendly, trainable, often low-shedding.
  • Labradoodle — Labrador Retriever x Poodle. The original designer doodle, energetic and adaptable.
  • Bernedoodle — Bernese Mountain Dog x Poodle. Gentle-giant temperament with reduced shedding.
  • Cavapoo — Cavalier King Charles Spaniel x Poodle. Small, calm, excellent for apartments.
  • Sheepadoodle — Old English Sheepdog x Poodle. Playful and sturdy with a panda coat.
  • Aussiedoodle — Australian Shepherd x Poodle. High-energy, brilliant, often heterochromatic eyes.

See our full Best Doodle Breeds for Families guide for in-depth coverage of all six doodle hybrids.

special.label: Considerations
special.heading: How to Choose the Right Hypoallergenic Breed
special.html:
Before selecting a hypoallergenic breed, it is essential to assess the severity of your allergies. People with very mild sensitivity may find that almost any low-shedding breed works well for them, while those with more significant reactions should consider spending time with multiple dogs of their preferred breed before committing. Visiting a breeder or reputable rescue and spending an hour or two around the dogs — ideally in an indoor setting — can give you a good indication of how your body responds. Consult with an allergist if you are unsure about the severity of your dog allergy.

Grooming is a critical consideration for hypoallergenic breeds. The tradeoff for a low-shedding coat is often more intensive grooming requirements. Poodles, Bichon Frises, and Maltese need professional grooming every 6–8 weeks to prevent matting and maintain coat health. Portuguese Water Dogs and Lagotto Romagnolos need regular brushing at home. Hairless breeds like the Xolo and Chinese Crested require skin care including moisturizer and sun protection. Factor the cost and time of grooming into your decision — it is a real and ongoing expense with most low-shedding breeds.

Think about temperament and lifestyle compatibility alongside allergen concerns. A Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier's low-shedding coat won't help if the dog's high energy doesn't match your lifestyle. A Spanish Water Dog needs a job or sport to stay mentally satisfied. The Maltese and Chinese Crested are better suited to quiet households than active families. Use the allergen-friendliness of a breed as a filter, not the sole criterion — the right dog for your life is one that matches both your allergy needs and your activity level, living situation, and desire for companionship.

faq.q: Is there truly a 100% hypoallergenic dog?
faq.a: No — every dog produces the Can f 1 protein that triggers most human dog allergies, found in saliva, urine, and dander. However, breeds that shed minimally and have low dander production significantly reduce the amount of allergen in the environment compared to heavy-shedding breeds. Many allergy sufferers find they can live comfortably with low-shedding breeds even if they react to other dogs. The best approach is to spend time with the specific breed — and ideally the specific dog — before making a commitment.

faq.q: Does bathing a dog reduce allergens?
faq.a: Yes, regular bathing can meaningfully reduce the amount of dander and allergen on a dog's coat and skin. Studies have shown that bathing a dog weekly can reduce airborne allergen levels in the home. Using a gentle, dog-appropriate shampoo is important to avoid drying out the skin, which can actually increase dander production. Keeping the dog out of the bedroom, using HEPA air purifiers, and vacuuming with a HEPA-filter vacuum are also highly effective strategies for managing dog allergens in the home.

Poodle mixes like Labradoodles, Goldendoodles, and Cockapoos are often marketed as hypoallergenic, but this is unreliable. Because they are crossbreeds, puppies can inherit the coat type of either parent — a Goldendoodle might have a tightly curled Poodle coat or a straight, heavy-shedding Golden Retriever coat. There is no way to guarantee which coat a mixed-breed puppy will have. If you specifically need a low-allergen dog, a purebred from a consistently low-shedding breed like the Poodle or Portuguese Water Dog is a more reliable choice than a Doodle mix.
